newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S SECOND OIL REFINERY STEPS UP OPERATIONS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S SECOND OIL REFINERY STEPS UP OPERATIONS.

text.p: Bulgaria's second oil refinery, Plama, is recovering production after its partial sale to local oil trader Euroenergy, a company official said on Thursday.
Euroenergy's Atanas Kolarov said his firm had sealed deals for crude oil supplies from Russia and northern Africa.
He did not specify who the suppliers were.
"We have fixed a schedule for oil deliveries with our suppliers and we expect the first shipment by the end of the month," Kolarov told Reuters.
Last month Euroenergy bought 75 percent of Plama for some 62 million levs. The new owner is expected to invest around 12 billion levs in the refinery in next five years.
Plama, located in the northern town of Pleven, stopped production last November due to a lack of funds to buy crude.

Kolarov said the Plama refinery, which produces mainly lubricating oils and meets some 80 percent of the country's needs, was speeding up its technical processes since September in a bid to get back to normal work.
The refinery had been among 64 state firms slated for closure in the government's reform programme agreed with international lending institutions aimed at eliminating loss-making enterprises.
The refinery's debts to domestic banks amount to around $60 million and seven billion levs.
The 25-year-old refinery signed an agreement in 1993 with France's Elf Aquitaine SA to sell lubricating oils for ships.
